hook: This is a short, gentle entry built almost entirely around one conversation. The object is an ordinary graphing calculator recovered from a condemned school, and the fun lies in how it talks: all caps, barely any punctuation, and a personality that leaks through every reply. Go in expecting charm rather than dread.
whyItMatters: SCP-168 shows how little an entry needs to make a sapient object memorable: one interview, one short report, and a name scratched inside a casing. Nothing here is a threat to be managed, which makes it a nice palate cleanser among files about hostile talking things. It is also a neat case of containment procedures being shaped by what an anomaly wants rather than by how dangerous it is.
thingsToNotice:
Read the containment procedures again after the interview: the calculator is propped up facing an open window because it complained about being left in a dark room. It answers 2+2 at once but needs twelve seconds for 264÷8 because long division is hard, as if it is working the problem out by hand like a pupil. It can state its age down to the second but had never been asked before.

The quiet sadness sits in the Eric lines: it keeps repeating that he was nice and hopes the forgetful boy will come back for it, though it was found in an abandoned school. The only incident in the file is the next morning's overturned table and a screen calling the doctor a jerk for leaving it in the dark, a sulk rather than a breach, and it is that tantrum that got it the room with a view.
